tagline.text: Misamis Oriental's highest peak, with mossy ridge forest and a natural park to trek

location.label: Location
location.text: Gingoog City, Balingasag, Claveria and Medina, Misamis Oriental

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱2,000~4,000 (estimate for 2 days and 1 night from Cagayan de Oro; transport, lodging and guide to be confirmed locally)

children.text: Mount Balatukan rises to about 2,450 m and is the highest volcanic mountain in Misamis Oriental. The mossy ridge-forest trek from Gingoog City is its best-known route, and the whole mountain lies within a natural park designated in 2007.
Mount Balatukan is a compound stratovolcano in the east of Misamis Oriental province in northern Mindanao, jutting out toward the Bohol Sea. According to Wikipedia it stands about
high, the tallest point in the province. The summit holds a triangular caldera about
15 km
long and about

wide at its widest, and the Balatocan River drains from it. No historical eruptions are recorded; weak fumarolic activity survives in heavily eroded form, and PHIVOLCS classifies the volcano as inactive.

The entire mountain belongs to the Mount Balatukan Range Natural Park, established on March 6, 2007 by Proclamation No. 1249. The park covers about 8,040 hectares with a separate buffer zone, and spans Gingoog City and the three municipalities of Claveria, Medina and Balingasag. The forest is intact enough to be mentioned as Philippine Eagle habitat, and it is ranked as a Key Biodiversity Area (KBA) and an Important Bird Area (IBA). The park is said to contain waterfalls, caves, seventeen rivers and Baantawan Lake.

The route most often written about starts at Sitio San Isidro in Barangay Lunotan, Gingoog City. From there you walk the road to the Jamboree campsite, then follow a thickly moss-covered ridge forest up toward the summit area. The highest point is called Rosas Pandan Peak, and the prominent peak next to it is Pamalihi Peak. Because the range is long and reportedly has higher, still unexplored points, it is closer to a mountain group than a single peak.

That said, this is not a popular mountain with tourist facilities. I could not find an official entrance-fee schedule or an official guide system, and the trail is only simply marked. In 2020 there was a news report of three hikers who got lost in the forest and were rescued after three days. It suits people who are confident with fitness and map reading, and who contact the local village and the natural park office in advance to confirm how to enter. In February 2026 it was reported that DENR is pushing for this natural park to become the province's first ASEAN Heritage Park, and in August-September 2026 it was reported to have been endorsed for the designation, but it still awaits final approval by the ASEAN Ministerial Meeting on the Environment, so it is not yet confirmed.
At about
it is the highest in the province, with a prominence of about
. Because it juts out toward the Bohol Sea, views should be good in clear weather, but most of the ridge is forested, so open viewpoints are limited.

A 2011 hiking account described the ridge trail as passing through very mossy, pristine forest. A 2020 traverse account also describes mostly forest trail with grassy pockets opening at higher elevations, and compared it to the Kitanglad Range in Mindanao.

blocks.title: Triangular caldera and the Balatocan River

children.text: The summit caldera is about
15 km
across at its longest. The Balatocan River starts in the caldera and flows around the mountain, so the whole mountain acts as one large water source.

Designated in 2007, the natural park protects about 8,040 hectares with a separate buffer zone. The forest is known as home to rare wildlife such as the Philippine Eagle, so it is also worth visiting for birds and forest.

blocks.title: Pamalihi Peak and Rosas Pandan Peak

children.text: The summit is Rosas Pandan Peak, and the nearby peak is Pamalihi Peak. The 2020 traverse account started before dawn, passed the high camps, climbed Pamalihi Peak, and followed the ridge down to San Isidro.

blocks.title: Forest camping and the partial traverse

children.text: Accounts mention small campsites and a place to get water along the way. A traverse that climbs from San Isidro and descends toward Balingasag is said to be possible, but it needs one more day.

In Bukidnon belief, the souls of the dead travel to this mountain to be judged. Good souls rise to heaven from the summit, while evil souls atone in the river. Indigenous communities live in the forest and some serve as forest guardians, so be respectful when photographing and camping.

blocks.title: Sipaka Point at the northern tip

children.text: At the mountain's northernmost tip, Mount Sipaka, a cinder cone about
high, juts out as a small peninsula. The coastal road between Balingasag and Gingoog runs along the northern edge of the mountain, so you can see its outline from the car.

items.title: 2-day, 1-night summit trek
items.subtitle: From the San Isidro trailhead; an example based on a 2011 account

children.text: Take a bus to Gingoog from the Agora Terminal in Cagayan de Oro. You reach Gingoog City in mid-afternoon. Bus schedules may change, so check locally.

From Gingoog, take a motorcycle taxi (habal-habal) to Sitio San Isidro in Barangay Lunotan. Let the village head (barangay captain) and others know you are going up, and arrange a homestay or lodging.
Leave San Isidro and walk the road for about
15 minutes
to reach the Jamboree campsite. After that the mossy ridge forest trail begins. Reportedly the trees carry markings and red ribbons.
Pass a water source about halfway and a dried waterfall, then reach the summit area. The 2011 account took about
5 hours 30 minutes
Descend by the same route, reach the Jamboree campsite around 4 p.m., then return to Cagayan de Oro via Gingoog. If you are not strong, it is safer to add another night.
These times come from one hiker's account in 2011. Trail conditions and transport may have changed, so confirm the current situation locally before planning.

items.title: Pre-dawn one-day traverse
items.subtitle: Kalagonoy to San Isidro, about 12 hours

children.text: According to a 2020 account, the hike started at 1 a.m. from Barangay Kalagonoy. This is a schedule for very experienced hikers.
Reach the high camps, rest briefly, then climb Pamalihi Peak.
Follow the forest ridge down to the Boy Scout camp at San Isidro. The whole trip reportedly took about
12 hours
There are direct flights from Manila (NAIA) to Laguindingan International Airport (CGY) in Cagayan de Oro. Airlines and times change often, so check when booking.
You can also go through Butuan (BXU) airport. It is reportedly about 1 to 1.5 hours from Gingoog, but check flights locally.
Buses to Gingoog run from the Agora Bus Terminal in Cagayan de Oro. By map data, Gingoog is about
2 hours
northeast of Cagayan de Oro.
Check fares and schedules locally.
You need a separate transfer from the airport to the city center, so allow plenty of time.
From Gingoog to San Isidro (Barangay Lunotan), motorcycle taxis (habal-habal) are the usual way.
Trailheads at Kalagonoy, the Civoleg community and Balingasag are also known, but check how to reach them locally.

Mount Balatukan lies in eastern northern Mindanao, so rain can fall all year and the high forest is always wet. There is no clear dry season, so aim for relatively clear months and always check the forecast.

In rain the mossy forest and ridge trail become slippery and leeches increase. On foggy days it is easy to lose the trail markings, so ask locally before you set out and postpone if the weather is bad.

A 2011 account says there are local homestays in the San Isidro village. Do not expect restaurants or convenience stores, so buy meals, water and emergency food in Cagayan de Oro or Gingoog town before you go. Gingoog town has lodging and restaurants, so you can also sleep in town the night before and head to the trailhead before dawn.

After the hike, the easiest plan is to return to Cagayan de Oro and finish with a warm meal and a shower. If you have time, drive slowly around Gingoog town and the coastal road and photograph the northern outline of the mountain. Cagayan de Oro has many restaurants and hotels, which makes it a good base before and after. If you camp, carry out all your trash and be careful with fire and with damaging trees inside the natural park.
The basics are to register at the barangay office (the Lunotan village head, for example) before going up and ask about the safety situation.
The 2011 account advised contacting the military detachment to confirm that no operations are under way. Always check the current peace and order situation.
There are leeches, so bring long socks, leech repellent and a waterproof jacket.
A water source is said to exist along the way, but the amount is uncertain, so carry plenty.
Bring a GPS track, offline maps and a power bank. Route marking is only tree marks and red ribbons.
A round trip to the summit can take about
10 hours
or more, so an early start is recommended.

The forest is thick and wet, so a headlamp, warm clothing and a waterproof pack cover are needed. Keeping dry clothes to change into in a separate plastic bag helps greatly with keeping warm after the descent.
This is Indigenous community territory, so respect the guidance of the village and the forest guardians.
I could not confirm an official entry procedure or guide system. Before departing, contact the DENR natural park office, the relevant local governments and the barangay, and avoid hiking alone.
In January 2020 three hikers got lost in the forest and were rescued three days later.
In 2012 one mountaineer turned back because of security concerns. Check the latest security information.
In rain the mossy ridge is very slippery and the fog thickens. Do not climb if the weather is bad.
Phone signal may be weak, so tell the village and your family your plan.
Entry fees and permit rules may change, so check the latest announcements.
The departure and return city for the Balatukan hike. It is about
2 hours
by bus to Gingoog.
A highland leisure area south of Cagayan de Oro, good to add before or after the hike.
A nearby attraction toward Iligan, outside Misamis Oriental, that needs a separate itinerary.
The gateway city to the San Isidro trailhead. Arrange lodging, meals and habal-habal here.
